question_text: A 50-year-old man is brought in by ambulance to the emergency department with difficulty breathing and speaking. His wife reports that he might have swallowed a fishbone. While taking his history the patient develops a paroxysmal cough. Visualization of his oropharynx and larynx shows a fishbone lodged in the right piriform recess. After successfully removing the fishbone the patient feels comfortable, but he is not able to cough like before. Damage to which of the following nerves is responsible for the impaired cough reflex in this patient?
